speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are bringing in a newborn with yellowish skin discoloration; have they been feeding well, and is the yellowing spreading to their eyes or palms? REQUEST TEST: Total_Bilirubin, Direct_Bilirubin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The bilirubin results show a total of 7 mg/dL with an indirect fraction of 6.4 mg/dL. Is the baby more than 24 hours old, have they had any jaundice in previous siblings, and are they passing urine and stool normally?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby is 5 days old, exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours, and stooling/urinating normally. Given the total bilirubin of 7 mg/dL with a predominantly indirect fraction, this clinical picture is consistent with breast milk jaundice. Are there any signs of dehydration or poor weight gain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Yellowish discoloration of the skin. I also have Discoloration started from the face then spread to the trunk, Scleral icterus noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiological Jaundice of the Newborn. The clinical picture of a 5-day-old exclusively breastfed term infant with total bilirubin of 7 mg/dL (predominantly indirect), normal feeding and voiding, and jaundice spreading from the face to the trunk is consistent with benign physiological jaundice, likely with a contributing factor of breastfeeding jaundice. No further testing or intervention is currently indicated as the bilirubin level is well below the threshold for treatment.
